analysis.title: GS Malmstrom - Few Charts 18 Oct 2026
key_insights: S&P 500 is hovering around all-time highs while the market underneath is rewarding Quality stocks.
Quality in Europe is ending a long stretch of underperformance versus the market. US Quality is at 12-month highs after one of its strongest periods of outperformance.
Quality tends to outperform when earnings momentum weakens, which the market is expecting into next year. The European Quality premium to the market is now below its recent-year norm.

The AI trade was volatile this week. GS prime brokerage data showed the largest net selling of Global AI stocks in the past year after July, on Wednesday (Z score -2.8), driven by long and short sales at a 3.5 to 1 ratio.
Net allocation to Global AI stocks has fallen to 26.1% of total single-stock net, versus about 33% in June. The aggregate L/S ratio for Global AI stocks is 3.27, versus a June peak of 4.34.
US equity multiples have declined this year as bond yields rose, and equities usually struggle when yields rise sharply.
Corporate balance sheets face limited fundamental risk from higher rates. The rise in interest expense has been manageable and S&P 500 interest coverage (ex Financials) is historically high.
The equity market has downgraded its growth outlook, visible in Cyclicals versus Defensives.
High yield credit spreads have widened, especially for AI-related issuers.
The earnings boost from AI capex should fade going forward. The S&P 500 ex AI (SPXAII) has outperformed as AI stocks sold off, and the Momentum factor has unwound much of its recent gains.
earnings_insights: The report expects the earnings boost from AI capex to fade going forward. Quality outperforms when earnings momentum weakens, and the market is expecting weaker momentum into next year.
risk_factors: Rising bond yields are pressuring equity multiples.
Market growth expectations are being cut, with cyclicals lagging defensives.
High yield spreads are widening for AI-related issuers.
The earnings boost from AI capex is expected to fade.
Momentum and AI stocks are unwinding.
